* Toronto stocks ended lower after a volatile session on Wednesday * TSE 300 Index opened higher, but quickly turned negative amid inflation fears * 98 million shares traded
Toronto stocks ended lower after a volatile session on Wednesday, surrendering early gains as inflation fears gripped investors.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 17.48 points to close at 6791.02 in turnover of 98 million shares worth C$1.64 billion.

Canadian equities opened higher after the release of lower than expected U.S. producer price data. But the buoyant mood did not last long. "Everybody is saying even if producer prices are on negative side now, it doesn't mean inflation is gone," said Ira Katzin, an investment advisor with RBC Dominion Securities.
Skittish investors will get more economic data on Thursday with the release of U.S. consumer price figures.
"They (consumer prices) are not expected to rise too dramatically," Katzin said.
In today's action, interest-rate sensitive groups were among the nine of 14 sub-groups that ended lower. The decline was restrained by gains in precious metals and conglomerates.
Declining stocks outpaced advances 517 to 443, with 304 issues unchanged.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Repap Enterprises Inc was the heaviest trader, up 0.005 to 0.265 on volume of 6.5 million shares. Repap earlier announced the resignation of founder, chairman and chief executive George Petty.
* Among rate-sensitive stocks, BCE Inc fell 0.35 to 40.05 on 1.8 million shares. Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce dropped 0.35 to 37.85 on 1.3 million shares.
* Canadian Pacific Ltd jumped 1.30 to 42.30 after it agreed to acquire Contship Containers Ltd, which will boost CP Ships' total annual revenues to more than C$2 billion.
* Lumonics Inc sank 2.25 to 29.25 after only a modest rise in second-quarter earnings.
